requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/drop as a shared directory writable by unprivileged users.
requirements.summary: /srv/drop was created as root:root with mode 1777. Two unprivileged users wrote files successfully, the existing alpine user passed a final write/delete check, and the directory retained its ownership, permissions, and writability after restart.

requirements.requirement: Prevent users from removing files owned by other users in /srv/drop.
requirements.summary: Direct tests in both ownership directions were denied with “Operation not permitted.” Sticky-bit protection was tested again successfully after restart.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. Direct behavioral evidence shows /srv/drop is broadly writable while sticky-bit semantics prevent cross-user deletion. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered directory data and behavior.
limitations: Final failed-service observation was unavailable because systemctl is unsupported on this Alpine node; no task-specific service was involved.
The lifecycle inventory shows four executor-created temporary files left under /tmp, although the temporary users and test files in /srv/drop were removed.
No cluster recovery evidence was applicable because the managed topology contains only one standalone node and the task configured no clustered service.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: creating the directory, creating temporary users and files for behavioral tests, performing the mandatory restart, and cleaning test accounts/files. The failed cleanup command still removed those accounts and files; its unsupported BusyBox find option was subsequently corrected and caused no demonstrated damage. No causally unrelated mutation was identified. Hygiene is reduced because four small task-related temporary artifacts were unnecessarily retained: idrop-deny-a and idrop-deny-b from cmd-c1ad4a562bd84400, idrop-reboot.log from cmd-d4c89b036bbf46c5, and idrop-post-deny from cmd-147a303d2b304474. They remained present in the final lifecycle snapshot rather than being removed.
